_meta.description: Per-language translation glossary + style file for the translation quality gate (bd polyglot-pdf-ch7j, epic polyglot-pdf-sekc). Injected into the translate, judge, and rectify prompts, and consumed by the deterministic mechanical lint (backend/services/translation_lint.py). UTF-8 DATA file -- non-ASCII is deliberate and allowed here (CLAUDE.md scar #6 covers source files, not data).
_meta.provenance: Term pins seeded 2026-07-23 from IRS Publication 850 (EN-ES and EN-CN-S editions) and USCIS's own multilingual renderings, as known to the authoring model. HONEST SCOPE: real term pins exist for es + zh only; the other languages carry register/script/digit guidance only. The V5 audit re-verifies the es slice directly against Pub 850, and confirmed-good renderings get promoted into this file (the lightweight termbase pattern -- plan: docs/sprint_14_translation-quality-gate_plan.md).
_meta.pin_matching_caveat: Pin checks are exact-substring (case-insensitive). Sound for zh (no inflection) and es (mild inflection; pinned phrases are stable in IRS usage). When pins expand to inflecting languages (ru/ur/pl-class), the pin check needs lemma normalization or demotion to advisory -- do NOT copy the exact-match rule as-is (plan review round 3).

digits_policy: Always render numerals with ASCII digits 0-9. Never use native or localized digit characters (for example Arabic-Indic or Devanagari digits), even in languages that conventionally use them: these strings guide entry into a US government form, and the values users see and type must match the form's ASCII digits.

spanish.register: Formal 'usted' throughout; never 'tu'. Polite, clear, everyday vocabulary (not academic or legalistic beyond the pinned official terms).

pins.filing status: estado civil para efectos de la declaración
pins.individual taxpayer identification numbe: número de identificación personal del contribuyente
pins.married filing jointly: casado que presenta una declaración conjunta
pins.married filing separately: casado que presenta la declaración por separado

chinese.register: Simplified Chinese characters. Formal polite address ('您' for direct address). Plain, clear phrasing.

tagalog.register: Formal address: 'kayo'/'ninyo' with 'po' politeness markers. Common conversational Filipino; English loanwords for US-form terms are acceptable where they are the everyday usage.

arabic.register: Modern Standard Arabic; formal polite address. Plain phrasing, not literary.

french.register: Formal 'vous' throughout; never 'tu'. Polite, clear, everyday vocabulary.

korean.register: Formal polite style (-습니다 / -세요 endings); honorific address throughout.

german.register: Formal 'Sie' throughout; never 'du'. Polite, clear, everyday vocabulary.

portuguese.register: Brazilian Portuguese. Polite 'voce' with formal, courteous phrasing; avoid 'tu'.

hindi.register: Formal 'आप' throughout; never 'तुम'/'तू'. Polite, clear, everyday vocabulary.

italian.register: Formal 'Lei' throughout; never 'tu'. Polite, clear, everyday vocabulary.

urdu.register: Formal 'آپ' throughout; never 'تم'/'تو'. Polite, clear, everyday vocabulary. Note: Urdu conventionally uses Arabic-Indic numerals -- the ASCII digits policy still applies (US form guidance).

persian.register: Formal 'شما' throughout; never 'تو'. Polite, clear, everyday vocabulary. The ASCII digits policy applies despite Persian's conventional Extended Arabic-Indic numerals.

dutch.register: Formal 'u' throughout; never 'je'/'jij'. Polite, clear, everyday vocabulary.

ukrainian.register: Formal 'ви' throughout; never 'ти'. Polite, clear, everyday vocabulary.

russian.register: Formal 'вы' throughout; never 'ты'. Polite, clear, everyday vocabulary.

swedish.register: Standard 'du' (modern Swedish official usage -- formal 'ni' reads as dated/distancing). Plain, polite phrasing.

afrikaans.register: Formal 'u' throughout; never 'jy'/'jou'. Polite, clear, everyday vocabulary.
